title: What they said at the time

clips.q: AOL’s marketing clearly got out ahead of its technological capacity.
With 55 percent of the new company’s stock being controlled by AOL shareholders, I think AOL is in the driver’s seat.
clips.who: **An analyst at Raymond James**, quoted by CNET News.com on the day of the merger, Jan 10, 2000[^22]

clips.q: America Online recently has experienced declines in the number of U.S. subscribers, to approximately 26.5 million at December 31, 2002, and anticipates that it will experience further declines.
When we went public in 1992 we had less than 200,000 subscribers; a decade later the number was in the 25 million range.
clips.who: **Steve Case**, on Quora, as quoted by TechCrunch, Dec 2010[^24]

clips.q: Verizon’s vision is to provide customers with a premium digital experience based on a global multiscreen network platform.
clips.who: **Lowell McAdam**, Verizon chairman and CEO, on buying AOL, May 12, 2015[^15]

clips.q: AIM tapped into new digital technologies and ignited a cultural shift, but the way in which we communicate with each other has profoundly changed.
clips.who: **Michael Albers**, Oath, announcing the end of AIM, as quoted by The Verge, Oct 6, 2017[^27]

clips.q: what is usually described as the worst merger of all time
clips.who: **Fortune**, on the fifteenth anniversary of the deal, Jan 10, 2015[^31]

clips.q: AOL routinely evaluates its products and services and has decided to discontinue Dial-up Internet.
